content_list.content_text: Images of panic from another time: a man runs against the traffic, shouting: "They're after you! They're after all of us!" An old lady gives a nervous communist spy permission to kill her. A young woman kills her accomplice for the chance to open a metal box and unleash the hissing serpents of nuclear destruction.

information.contentText: The film withstood the scrutiny of the Kefauver Commission, which called it a film "designed to ruin young viewers", prompting director Aldrich to protest the Commission's conclusions. Despite initial critical distaste, it is considered one of the most important and influential film noirs of all time, with praise directed at its dark tone, its deconstruction of popular fiction archetypes and its twist ending.

content_list.content_text: These sequences come from three films of the mid-1950s: Pickup on South Street (1953), Kiss Me Deadly (1955) and Invasion of the Body Snatchers (1956), shown in American theaters during the country's most troubled era, capturing the psychological atmosphere of a nation in the age of the Cold War and McCarthyism. The arrival of the House Un-American Activities Committee (HUAC) in Hollywood in September 1947 left the studio heads trembling with fear. At a secret meeting at the Waldorf Astoria hotel in New York in November of that year, they adopted a policy of cooperation.

Often cited as the first Cold War film, The Iron Curtain (1948), directed by William Wellman (1896-1975), is a relatively sober story based on the real events of a spy ring in Canada. The political brutality present in many of the films that followed is reflected in titles such as The Red Menace (1949), directed by R.G. Springsteen (1904-1989), in which a war veteran is lured in by communist spies, or I Was a Communist for the FBI (1951), by Gordon Douglas (1907-1993), about an undercover agent infiltrating the Communist Party. With cheap budgets and no big stars, the studios' propaganda pieces seemed almost like an excuse.

information.contentTitle: Scenes from It Came from Outer Space (1953)
information.contentText: Patricia Bosworth, writing in 1992, considered It Came from Outer Space one of a series of anti-communist propaganda films from 1950s Hollywood in which "aliens from outer space serve as metaphors for the Soviet threat".

content_list.content_text: The Woman on Pier 13 (1949), whose original title was I Married a Communist until the studio decided to change it, directed by Robert Stevenson (1905-1986), was offered by Howard Hughes to several directors as a loyalty test. The absurdities of the screenplay are offset by Nicholas Musuraca's (1892-1975) noir-style cinematography and by the cast headed by Robert Ryan (1909-1973).

John Wayne (1907-1979) starred in Big Jim McLain (1952), directed by Edward Ludwig (1898-1982), as a gruff investigator for the House Un-American Activities Committee who uncovers a nest of communists in Hawaii (the poster's tagline: "He's a defender of the U.S. on a trail full of traps that leads him to the ends of the earth!").

quote.quote: Invasion of the Body Snatchers is one of the most popular and paranoid films of the golden age of American science fiction cinema
quote.author: Steven Jay Schneider on Invasion of the Body Snatchers

content_list.content_text: In the summer of 1947, newspapers reported that unidentified wreckage had been found in New Mexico, giving rise to the first wave of UFO paranoia. Alien invasion plots in science fiction films reflected Cold War anxieties. The Thing from Another World (1951), directed by Christian Nyby (1913-1993) but credited to producer Howard Hawks, shows blood-drinking aliens unwittingly brought to a research station in the Arctic. Its final line, "Watch the skies, everywhere!", could be read as a warning to the nation.

information.contentTitle: Scenes from Invasion of the Body Snatchers (1956)
information.contentText: "Invasion of the Body Snatchers" was Don Siegel's only foray into science fiction. It used no special effects, monsters, alien spaceships, cosmic weapons or death scenes, only the strength of the screenplay, building a climate of paranoia solely through the power of suggestion. "For never has a work of science fiction been so tense and claustrophobic, nor has one ever exploited a society's paranoias as well as Invasion of the Body Snatchers".

content_list.content_text: It Came from Outer Space (1953) is more ambiguous: the aliens are relatively benign, but they temporarily inhabit human bodies. Invasion of the Body Snatchers (1956), with its hordes of aliens imitating their human hosts, can be seen as a metaphor for the communist threat or for the frightening American conformity under McCarthyism.

Invaders from Mars (1953) was less ambiguous: a little boy watches his parents being turned into robotic-voiced zombies by evil green parasites (read "reds"); then the aliens are annihilated by the virtuous forces of the U.S. Army.

Jack Arnold's (1916-1992) The Incredible Shrinking Man (1957) is the most touching metaphor for mid-20th-century America's jitters. A Los Angeles businessman notices that he is beginning to shrink - an irreversible consequence of nuclear contamination. On his journey toward disappearance, he ends up living in a dollhouse that mimics his own suburban home and faces his final struggle for survival in the basement, a speck amid the debris of American life.

information.contentTitle: Scenes from The Incredible Shrinking Man (1957)
information.contentText: The film verges on surrealism and black humor, but it doesn't seem to be intentional. The action scenes are considered quite imaginative, and the strange relationship that forms between the lead couple is one of the high points of the screenplay.

content_list.content_text: In the 1960s, it seemed possible that some of the political ghosts might be exorcised. John Frankenheimer's (1930-2002) The Manchurian Candidate (1962) portrayed a McCarthy-like senator as a buffoon used to bring about the communist domination of the United States, and Emile de Antonio's (1920-1989) Point of Order (1964) used television footage of the Army-McCarthy hearings to reveal the truth about McCarthyism. By then, the Cuban Missile Crisis and the Kennedy assassination meant that the fears of the 1950s had taken another form.

movies.title: It Came from Outer Space
movies.overview: Author & amateur astronomer John Putnam and schoolteacher Ellen Fields witness an enormous meteorite come down near a small town in Arizona, but Putnam becomes a local object of scorn when, after examining the object up close, he announces that it is a spacecraft, and that it is inhabited...

movies.title: Invasion of the Body Snatchers
movies.overview: A small-town doctor learns that the population of his community is being replaced by emotionless alien duplicates.

movies.title: Angel of Evil
movies.overview: Set in Italy in the 1970s, VALLANZASCA is the true story of the Italian underworld’s most infamous outlaw. A criminal by age 9, Renato Vallanzasca grew up to become the country’s most notorious mobster before the age of 27. Vallanzasca and his gang wrested control of the Milan underworld with a string of high profile robberies, kidnappings and murders. In the process, he captivated the public and earned the nickname ‘il bel Renè’ – for his devilish charm and handsome face. Arrested multiple times, his daring escapes from prison enraged the government, angered his rivals and fed his legend.

movies.original_title: I Was a Communist for the FBI
movies.title: I Was a Communist for the FBI
movies.overview: A fact-based story about a man who posed as an American Communist for years as part of a secret plan to infiltrate their organization.

movies.title: The Incredible Shrinking Man
movies.overview: While on a boating trip, Scott Carey is exposed to a radioactive cloud. Nothing seems amiss at first, but several months later Scott realizes that he's shrunk in height by several inches. He sees a doctor, who admits that he's baffled. As Scott continues to shrink, decreasing to three feet tall, he becomes bitter, and lashes out at his wife, Louise. He begins to fear a cure will never be found -- since even as he becomes a national sensation, he's still shrinking.

movies.title: Kiss Me Deadly
movies.overview: One evening, Hammer gives a ride to Christina, an attractive hitchhiker on a lonely country road, who has escaped from the nearby lunatic asylum. Thugs waylay them and force his car to crash. When Hammer returns to semi-consciousness, he hears Christina being tortured until she dies. Hammer, both for vengeance and in hopes that "something big" is behind it all, decides to pursue the case.

movies.title: The Manchurian Candidate
movies.overview: Near the end of the Korean War, a platoon of U.S. soldiers is captured by communists and brainwashed. Following the war, the platoon is returned home, and Sergeant Raymond Shaw is lauded as a hero by the rest of his platoon. However, the platoon commander, Captain Bennett Marco, finds himself plagued by strange nightmares and soon races to uncover a terrible plot.

content_list.title: Timeline of Events from 1940 to 1959
content_list.description: Asian cinema gains even more prominence with the release of several masterpieces. Film noir emerges and musicals continue to shine on the big screen. The Western holds on to its reign as one of the most popular genres, and one of the most important movements in cinema takes place in France: the French New Wave.
